title: arXiv Trending Physics — latest announcement batch: 16 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred selection of notable recent papers, not a measured popularity ranking; newly announced papers have little citation history from which to measure popularity.

sections.title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay D^0 to gamma omega
sections.abstract: BESIII reports the first observation of this radiative charm decay, with a measured branching fraction of (2.12 ± 0.40_stat ± 0.25_syst) × 10^-5.
sections.claimed_result: Using e+e- data at 3.773 GeV, the authors measure the branching fraction and argue it supports long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; BESIII e+e- collision data analyzed with a Particle Transformer classifier
sections.unique_caveat: The rate has statistical and systematic uncertainties; the long-distance-dynamics conclusion is an interpretation, not a separately isolated mechanism.

sections.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
sections.abstract: The Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration computes the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to muon g-2, obtaining a full-HVP value of (714.9 ± 8.1) × 10^-10 after applying the WP25 leading isospin-breaking correction.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find their Standard Model prediction consistent with the latest Fermilab measurement and strengthen tension with pre-CMD3 data-driven dispersive determinations.
sections.evidence_type: computational; N_f=2+1+1 Wilson-clover twisted-mass lattice QCD with four lattice spacings and spatial sizes up to about 7.7 fm
sections.unique_caveat: The headline full-HVP number incorporates an external WP25 isospin-breaking correction; continuum and finite-volume extrapolations and the isospin-symmetric setup remain important.

sections.title: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
sections.abstract: Thermal Hall transport, constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, assigns the larger superconducting gap in CeRu2 to heavy electron sheets and the smaller gap to hole sheets.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer gap scales near 13 K and 8 K and assign the larger gap to the heavy Ce 4f electron sheets using the measured transport response in a two-band framework.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; thermal-Hall and longitudinal heat transport, specific heat, and normal-state magnetotransport in CeRu2 single crystals
sections.unique_caveat: The band assignment relies on a compensated two-band transport picture and a two-gap Bardeen–Rickayzen–Tewordt analysis; it concerns one material.

sections.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
sections.abstract: An evolutionary search in which LLMs propose circuits and an independent evaluator scores them reduces Toffoli and qubit counts against reported baselines in seven of eight tested tasks.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion and improved resource trade-offs; these are algorithmic benchmarks, not evidence of quantum advantage on hardware.
sections.evidence_type: computational; evolutionary LLM circuit proposals evaluated on eight tasks
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the selected tasks and cost metrics; no experimental quantum-hardware validation or general practical speedup is reported in the abstract.

sections.title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
sections.abstract: Comparing gallium capture results with solar-neutrino source strengths calibrated through neutrino–electron scattering, the authors find agreement rather than an anomaly.
sections.claimed_result: The authors compare 66.1 ± 3.1 SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO with solar-source strengths of 67.5 +1.4/-1.1 SNU, concluding this comparison is not anomalous.
sections.evidence_type: observational; analysis of published gallium capture rates and solar-neutrino source strengths calibrated using standard-model neutrino–electron scattering
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion depends on solar-neutrino source-strength calibration and analyzes existing rates rather than directly remeasuring gallium cross section or detector efficiency.

sections.title: Projected sensitivity of a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate comagnetometer to proton monopole-dipole interactions
sections.abstract: The authors project that an upgraded 87Rb spinor-BEC comagnetometer could improve direct laboratory sensitivity to proton monopole–dipole interactions by several orders of magnitude.
sections.claimed_result: For a proposed bismuth-germanate source mass, the authors project a coupling reach near 2×10^-22 after planned upgrades and 3×10^-24 at the projection-noise limit for 100 μm range; these are forecasts, not new force limits.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; sensitivity calculations based on demonstrated 87Rb spinor-BEC magnetometry/comagnetometry and proposed apparatus upgrades
sections.unique_caveat: Reach depends on planned improvements, source-mass positioning, magnetic environment, noise assumptions, and integration time; the projection-noise-limit value is not demonstrated.
